subject: Re: POC scope & success metrics — alignment and next steps

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Jensen <michael.jensen@atlasai.com>
Cc: Rebecca Cole <rebecca.cole@atlasai.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & ask after today's call

Michael — thanks for the clear ask. Internal cc: Mina (SE) and Lauren (CS) who will drive technical onboarding and SLOs. Below is a concise POC success slate and a proposed plan — happy to iterate.

POC objective: validate Redwood inference for Atlas AI's extraction pipeline at representative scale and acceptable cost/latency while preserving labeling-quality (>92% on your metric).

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p50 < 180 ms, p95 < 350 ms for 512-token requests on our optimized c2-medium serving profile.
- Throughput: sustained 200 qps with <10% tail amplification during burst windows (10s bursts).
- Cost: average per-token cost <= $0.0006 (end-to-end including batching); demonstrate expected monthly spend extrapolation.
- Quality: end-to-end extraction F1 >= 0.92 measured against your gold set (we'll use the sample workload you provide).
- Reliability: <1% error rate (timeouts/500s) across the window and graceful fallback to smaller variant without data leakage.

Proposed 3-week timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): exchange sample traffic + SOC2 contact. Redwood provides POC proposal + onboarding checklist (attached).
- Week 1: sandbox ingest, model selection and baseline run (SE-led).
- Week 2: performance tuning (batching/kv-caching), latency/throughput ramp, cost model draft.
- Week 3: acceptance run, quality verification, and operational handoff (CS-led).

Recommended owners:
- Redwood AE: Dylan Brooks — commercial coordination and scope decisions.
- Redwood SE: Mina Haddad — workload onboarding, model selection, run optimization.
- Redwood CS/Onboarding: Lauren Bishop — acceptance testing and runbook handoff.
- Atlas AI owner: Michael Jensen — sample dataset, target quality metric, final acceptance sign-off.

Next steps:
1) Please send the sample traffic file (anonymized) and the gold labels by EOD Friday.
2) We'll return a short POC proposal doc and a tentative Dev/Test schedule by Monday.

Attaching: redwood-poc-proposal.pdf (proposal & checklist).

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — this looks actionable. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Quality metric: we'll send a gold set and specify that F1 on entity extraction is primary; target is >= 0.92 but we can accept a 0.90 floor if cost savings are significant.
- Traffic profile: daytime steady 120 qps, peak spikes to 400 qps for ~30s every hour; we'll attach a 24-hour anonymized trace.
- Can you confirm how you measure per-token cost (model compute + infra vs Redwood list price)? We need the extrapolated monthly cost at both baseline and optimized settings.
- SOC2: we'll upload the questionnaire to the Drive link you provided.

Also curious: for caching and batching, what assumptions do you need from our side (e.g., request idempotency, max accept length) to get the performance numbers you listed?

Rebecca
Senior Product Lead | Atlas AI

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rebecca Cole <rebecca.cole@atlasai.com>, Michael Jensen <michael.jensen@atlasai.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & ask after today's call

Appreciate the quick clarifications and the traffic file — that's exactly what we need. Short answers and next steps: 

Per-token cost: our baseline estimate will show compute + infra amortized across tokens (the number we'll share in the proposal). We'll also model an "optimized" estimate assuming quantized model variant + batching (we'll show both).

Caching/batching assumptions:
- We assume idempotent requests (replayable) and a reasonably stable prompt prefix so prefix-KV caching is effective; please flag any per-request unique session state beyond user input.
- Max request length: we'll plan for 512 tokens; if your average is >512, call that out so we can size kernels and memory.

Immediate next steps (concrete):
1) Redwood (Mina) will load the sample trace into a sandbox and run a smoke set on Monday.
2) Redwood will produce a one-page cost/latency comparison (baseline vs optimized) and a simple acceptance checklist by EOD Monday.
3) Atlas to confirm final acceptance metric and sign the small POC SOW (attached) when ready.

I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Monday afternoon with Mina and Lauren included — will send the invite.

Thanks — looking forward.
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
